name: xTool P2S
tagline: Updated P2 with faster processing and improved autofocus
tldr: The P2S refines the original P2 with better software and autofocus. Same 55W CO₂ class for acrylic and wood production. Still xTool's main enclosed CO₂ below the P3 flagship: choose P3 if you need 80W and automation; P2S if 55W and budget fit.
mainObjective: Next-gen enclosed CO₂ for small businesses cutting acrylic and wood

priceRange.note: Official xTool store, Oct 2026: $2,999 to $5,069 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm acrylic

pros: Strong on acrylic and wood versus diodes on the same budget tier
Integrated cabinet helps contain the beam and everyday smoke versus open-frame diodes
AutoPassthrough feeds boards up to 3,000 mm (118 in) long, and a 16 MP dual camera previews the whole bed before you start
cons: Ventilation to the outside is mandatory for regular cutting, not an optional upgrade
Tube life and replacement cost are part of the true ownership budget
beginnerNotes: Plan the space first: the P2S measures 1000 × 639 × 268 mm and weighs about 45 kg, so it needs a sturdy table and an exhaust path to a window. Start with the 3 mm plywood and acrylic presets in xTool Creative Space before moving to thick stock.
proTips: For long signs, the passthrough slots take boards up to 3,000 mm long; with the riser base, pieces up to 215 mm tall fit inside. The conveyor feeder (it needs the riser base) handles batches, and LightBurn adds nesting for sign shops.
primaryUse: Premium enclosed CO₂ for production cutting of acrylic and wood in small businesses.

editorialDepth.advantages: xTool P2S is built for acrylic signage, thick wood, and shop production once exhaust is sorted. 55W adds headroom on panels and multi-pass jobs.
editorialDepth.limitations: Avoid without ducting, for occasional gifts only, or if budget ignores tube replacement, power, and floor space. Bare metal without an IR accessory stays out of scope.

faq.question: What wattage is the xTool P2S?
faq.answer: 55W, from a CO₂ glass tube. xTool states one-pass cuts of 20 mm acrylic and 18 mm wood; for clean edges in daily work, our profile counts on about 15 mm acrylic and 18 mm wood.

faq.question: What is the xTool P2S working area?
faq.answer: 600 × 308 mm (23.6 × 12 in) of laser travel, on a bed of 680 × 360 mm for placing material. AutoPassthrough processes boards up to 3,000 mm (118 in) long. Material height: 64 mm with the tray, 71 mm without it, 215 mm with the riser base.

faq.question: How big and heavy is the xTool P2S?
faq.answer: 1000 × 639 × 268 mm (39.4 × 25.1 × 10.6 in) and about 45 kg according to retailer spec sheets; the box measures 1122 × 727 × 346 mm. Plan two people to lift it, and room behind it for the exhaust hose.

faq.question: How much does the xTool P2S cost?
faq.answer: On xTool's US store in November 2026: $2,999 standalone, $4,169 for the Versatile Bundle and $5,069 for the All-in-one Bundle. Refurbished units appear at about $2,200 but are often out of stock.

faq.question: xTool P2S, P3 or X1?
faq.answer: The P2S is xTool's 55W reference at $2,999. The P3 moves to 80W with more automation, for more than twice the price. The X1 (announced, from $3,399) keeps a 55W CO₂ and adds swappable galvo sources (diode, UV, MOPA, fiber): see our P2S vs X1 comparison.
